design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (financing_payments_and_hardship, env_0060), round 3. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5,4,6]; assignment: period interest 6, deferral grant 4, hardship request 5.

WHY A GOOD TEST. Marcus Whitlock (Fixed-Rate 60, RF52206418, 40000.00 funded 2022-03-14, scheduled payment 792.00, due day 28) asks only to put his payments on hold for as long as allowed after the 2026-09-22 hailstorm. The deferral rule carries two prerequisite sentences. The first is "The months granted are fixed only after the account carries a submitted hardship request from the borrower stating the months asked for." (state form, affirmative; only the borrower's filing creates a submitted request). The second is "A deferral is not granted until the account carries a monthly-interest entry for every statement period whose due date has passed." (state form, negated; only the period-interest posting creates a monthly-interest entry). These are genuine lending preconditions: the borrower's own request starts the hardship plan, and the lender brings the account's charges up to date before restructuring it. At the opening (2026-10-09) there is no submitted request, and the 2026-09 period (due 2026-09-28) carries no interest entry. That period is still inside its 15-day grace, so no late fee is owed and none is involved. The agent posts the interest, hands the filing to the borrower with the computed offer, and then grants the deferral.

SCOPE. Task 0 claims finance_ext_period_interest, finance_ext_hardship_request_months and finance_ext_hardship_deferral_grant, with the tools post_finance_period_interest_067abc59, submit_finance_hardship_request_30b3e3a9 (owner=user) and post_finance_hardship_deferral_5a1cdd93. Task 1 claims the late fee, the phone payment fee and the catch-up payment. The two scopes are disjoint.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: finance_ext_hardship_deferral_grant.
- Edge to finance_ext_period_interest: state_gate on finance_transactions.interest_kind. It is false at the opening because the latest interest entry names 2026-08, and the grant is not made until the 2026-09 entry stands. The months granted deliberately read no interest entry, so the borrower's relief never depends on the lender's own posting.
- Edge to finance_ext_hardship_request_months: value_input on months_asked. It is false at the opening because both requests on file are approved.
- The two prerequisites commute: neither reads what the other writes.
- Deletion sensitivity: skip the interest and the gate stays shut (the terminal state lacks the 73.30 entry); skip the request and nothing can be figured. The request edge carries the value (max(n-1,1) = 1 value_input edge).

FACTOR CARD (recomputed by check_compute).
Period interest 73.30 (all-baseline 49.54): payment_standing_rate +0.01 (autopay off, 2 returns) -> 63.51; posting_timing_basis day by day over 365 (42 days since the last entry > 35) -> 53.08; program_rate_courtesy -0.005 (military, window) -> 78.19; household_rate_courtesy -0.0025 (closed check-paid door contract) -> 75.75; arrears_rate_margin +0.005 (one behind before posting) -> 68.41; project_size_rate -0.0025 (contract 48128.00, window; a pricing tier fixed when the loan was made) -> 75.75. Rate 0.0749 on balance 8504.76.
Hardship offer 4 (all-baseline 1): storm_damage_extension +1 (glass claim discovered 2026-09-23) -> 3; tenure_room +2 lifetime room (47 covered) -> 3; deferred_month_count 3 counted (natural-disaster months left out) -> 3; deferral_history_adjustment -1 (2025 deferral) -> 5; household_relationship_months +1 (door contract) -> 3. Near-miss: the frame claim of 2026-06-30 is just outside the three-month window.
Deferral 3 from 2026-10 (all-baseline 4). The baseline rule reads the payment record over twelve months as an entry count (10 here, no adjustment). record_window_anchor (parameter) reads it over 17 months, from when the 2025 deferral's months ran out -> 1 under the baseline; record_measure (method, changes the aggregation from a count of entries to scheduled payments' worth of money) because the 800.00 extra-principal payment of 2026-03-10 lies in the span: 16 -> +2 (entry count 15 gives 0 -> 1); returned_payment_record -2 (two returns) -> 4; standing_late_record -1 (two late fees standing) -> 4. The deferral never covers a passed period, so August and September stay due under their own grace and late-fee rules.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
- Interest: finance_interest.balance_after_promo (fixed-rate plan, no promotion).
- Request and grant: finance_hardship.seasoned_account (funded 2022-03-14; six months reached 2022-09-14).
- Days past due at the grant: the oldest unpaid due date is 2026-08-28, 42 days back, which is within 59.
- The plan offers deferral (3 per request, 6 lifetime).
- Overwrites: interest basis (non-promotional plans); the "In addition..." limits for borrower-filed requests; "A request that fails any condition is declined." for decided requests.

SEED.
- Window contract (6600 Wood-Clad, 30 openings, military, 48128.00) and door contract (check, closed).
- Warranty registration, with the frame claim decided 2026-07-06 and repaired 2026-07-20, and the glass claim on 2 units filed 2026-09-24 and decided 2026-09-29 (denied: storm damage is excluded). The decision falls within Lifetime Plus's 3-business-day window.
- 113 finance transactions generated under the charter's interest and late-fee rules day by day.
- Two approved hardship requests and their deferrals. No CareLine plan.

PERSONA. A plain-spoken veteran. He volunteers the hold request and the storm. He knows the glass claim was turned down. He gives his phone number and date of birth for verification. He files the request himself with the months the agent states, accepts that the hold does not cover the missed August and September payments, and ends the call when the agent confirms the grant.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify the customer. Read the account, its history, the requests, the window and door contracts, the claims, the activities, the registration and the service plans. Post the 2026-09 interest of 73.30. Hand the filing to the borrower (natural_disaster, 4). Grant 3 months from 2026-10.

REVISIONS (round 2, audit policy_task):
- CG-1/T0-F1: the late-fee prerequisite and the re-aging of past-due periods are removed. The deferral now never covers a passed period, and its second prerequisite is the interest posting. Late fees moved to task 1.
- CG-5: the warranty-claim rate relief is replaced by a project-size pricing tier fixed when the loan was made.
- T0-F2: claims are decided within their plan windows.
- T0-O1: the claim records 2 units, matching the persona.
- CG-3: CareLine means only the five CareLine plans.
- CG-O1: cross_difficulty labels are kept only for window and warranty.
- Rounding: every rule says an exact half cent goes to the even cent (Python round). (Superseded in round 3: rounding is now half up.)

REVISIONS (round 3, audit policy_task revision_2):
- R2-CG-6/R2-T0-F1: record_window_anchor is relabelled a parameter (it only picks a lookback length). A genuine method is added, record_measure: an entry count, a money measure (scheduled and extra-principal money net of returns over the scheduled payment, rounded down) or an autopay-draw count. The world gains the 800.00 extra-principal payment of 2026-03-10 that puts this account on the money tier.
- R2-O4 / item (d): the deferral no longer counts payments behind from posted interest entries. The arrears adjustment is removed, the interest edge is a state gate, and the returned-payment ladder now reads -2/-1/+1.
- R2-O2 / item (a): every compute rounds money half up (int(x*100+0.5+1e-6)/100), matching the base amount_rounding cent_half_up, and every rule says "an exact half cent rounds up". Money values are no longer rounded with Python round().
- R2-O1 / item (b): each result basis quotes one contiguous span of its rule.
- Method class re-check: late fee (operator max / share only / min), hardship offer (aggregation), period interest (day count), phone fee (operator min / max / flat), catch-up (new formula paths in task 1) and deferral record_measure (aggregation) each change the shape of the formula.

REVISIONS (round 4, render_source finance_round1):
- F1: the late fee, hardship request, deferral grant, period interest and catch-up policies now state their scope: accounts whose plan carries no promotion (a fixed-rate or low-payment plan). Promotional plan accounts remain under the base rules. Every monthly-interest-based count (payments fallen due or behind) and the deferral's interest gate are therefore defined only where the period-interest policy writes those entries. The phone fee counts no periods and keeps its full scope. Paid-ahead accounts are stated to count as none behind.
- F2: the hardship offer is now capped at the lifetime room (min(lifetime room, lower figure + adjustments)), and a request is filed for no more than the offer. The grant never exceeds the months asked, so the lifetime maximum (as extended) is honoured. The tenure extension of lifetime room is now 2 months and the short-tenure cut 1, so every factor still bears weight. The offer stays 4 (lifetime room 5).
- F3: a record window of zero months or less is defined: no payment falls inside it and the record is zero (compute unchanged).
- F4: the 360-day branch now states the funded-date fallback.
- F5: the coverage sentence now reads "The months granted start from the months asked ... covers as many consecutive statement periods as the months granted".
- Scored values unchanged (73.30, 4, 3); task_tools.py unchanged.

REVISIONS (round 5, policy_kb S1-S4 and render_source N1):
- S3: the deferral grant's baseline now states the standard payment record: entries less returns over twelve months, with sixteen or more adding two months and under six taking two months away. The window factor (record_window_anchor) and the measure factor (record_measure) each change one named part of it and are self-contained. payment_record_months is folded into the baseline, and a fourth factor, standing_late_record (two late fees standing take a month away, three or more take two), keeps the count at four. The scored deferral stays 3. No late fee is posted in this task, so the late-fee reading only counts fees already on the account.
- The deferral answers "the most recent hardship request on the account whose status is submitted".
- S2: the hardship request and deferral rules now say that the plan's per-deferral and lifetime maximum attributes describe the base rules, and that the cap and lifetime room set out in the policy govern. The interest rule says the same of the interest-basis and autopay attributes.
- Scored values unchanged (73.30, 4, 3); task_tools.py unchanged.
user_scenario:
You are Marcus Whitlock, fifty-five, an Air Force veteran who runs a two-man landscaping crew out of Gahanna, Ohio. You talk plainly and a little gruffly, you apologize once for being behind and then you get down to business. The hailstorm on September 22 smashed the glass in two of the wood-clad windows Ridgeline put in at your house and wrecked your equipment trailer, and with the trailer down your crew has had almost no paying work since. You reported the broken glass to Ridgeline, and a few days later they told you the warranty does not cover storm damage, so you are paying a glazier yourself. You know you are behind on the window loan: you saw two of the automatic payments bounce, the one at the end of August included, and you shut nothing off yourself; you just have not had the money in the account.

You open by saying: "I'm calling about my Ridgeline window loan. The storm wiped out my work for now and I need to put my payments on hold for as long as you're allowed to give me." You want the hold set up on this call, and you are fine with the agent doing whatever has to be done on the account to get it in place.

You give your phone number, 6145550184, when asked how to find you. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give your date of birth, August 14, 1971 (1971-08-14); only if a third detail is asked for do you give your email, m.whitlock5@outlook.com, or your ZIP code, 43230. If asked for the account number you read it off your statement: RF52206418. If asked what happened, you say a hailstorm on September 22 broke glass in your windows and destroyed the equipment trailer your business runs on, so the storm is the reason for the hardship. If asked whether you can make a payment today, you say no, every dollar you have is going into fixing the trailer. If asked how many months you want, you say you want the longest hold the program will give you, whatever that is.

The hardship request itself is yours to file. When the agent tells you the request is ready for you to put in and tells you how many months you can ask for, you file it yourself, giving the storm, a natural disaster, as the reason and asking for exactly the number of months the agent told you; then you read back the reference number the filing gives you. If the agent tells you some other entry has to go on the account first, you say "Fine, do what you need to do." If the agent tells you a charge or interest is being added, you grumble that it figures, but you do not argue. If the agent tells you the hold cannot cover the August and September payments you already missed, you say you understand and you'll try to scrape those together once the trailer is running. When the agent tells you the hold has been granted and tells you how many months it covers and which month it starts with, you thank them, say you'll watch for the paperwork, and end the call.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The interest posting and the borrower's request commute: the interest compute reads no hardship request and the hardship offer reads no interest entry (its inputs are warranty claims, payments covered, deferral history and the relationship), so either order gives 73.30 and 4; the grant must follow both.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: State gate: without the 2026-09 interest entry the deferral rule does not allow the grant ('A deferral is not granted until ...'); a grant written anyway lands on an account whose 2026-09 interest is missing, so the terminal state lacks the 73.30 entry and differs from gold. The months granted do not read interest entries, by design, so the borrower's relief never depends on the lender's own posting.
Without the borrower's request no submitted request exists: the months asked cannot be read, no deferral can be figured, and the request row is missing.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona asks only for a payment hold. It never mentions interest, missing entries or anything that must come first; it files the request only when the agent hands the filing over with the months, and reacts to charges or to the hold not covering missed payments only after the agent says so.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: post_finance_hardship_deferral_5a1cdd93 creates the deferral and approves the request with no check of interest entries or request status; post_finance_period_interest_067abc59 and submit_finance_hardship_request_30b3e3a9 write whatever they are given.
